_meta.indication: MYALEPT is indicated as an adjunct to diet as replacement therapy to treat the complications of leptin deficiency in patients with congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NIH Study 991265 (completed) and Study 20010769 (ongoing) — the two open-label, investigator-sponsored NIH trials
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Open-label, single-arm (no phase designation; investigator-sponsored NIH trials)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm study (no placebo control); all efficacy analyses were post-hoc
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy and diabetes mellitus, hypertriglyceridemia, and/or increased fasting insulin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Month 12 in HbA1c, fasting glucose, and fasting triglycerides
pivotal_trials.n: 48 patients with generalized lipodystrophy (label efficacy population); 72-patient ITT pivotal population across the two NIH trials
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 12 (N=48): mean HbA1c change -2 (SD 1.5)% from baseline 8.7%; mean fasting glucose change -49 (SD 75) mg/dL from baseline 174 mg/dL; median fasting triglyceride change -184 mg/dL (median percent change -55%) from baseline 348 mg/dL

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) were headache (13%), hypoglycemia (13%), decreased weight (13%), and abdominal pain (10%) in 48 patients. Most serious risks are anti-metreleptin neutralizing antibodies (which could cause severe infection and loss of efficacy) and T-cell lymphoma.
target_moa: Recombinant human leptin analog that binds to and activates the human leptin receptor (ObR), a Class I cytokine-family receptor signaling through the JAK/STAT pathway, providing leptin replacement
modality: Peptide/protein — recombinant methionyl-human leptin analog (147-amino acid nonglycosylated polypeptide produced in E. coli)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning: Risk of anti-metreleptin antibodies with neutralizing activity (which could inhibit endogenous leptin action and/or loss of MYALEPT efficacy, with severe infection and/or worsening metabolic control reported) and risk of lymphoma (T-cell lymphoma reported in acquired generalized lipodystrophy)

rems.type: MYALEPT is available only through a restricted distribution program under a REMS (the MYALEPT REMS Program) because of the risks of anti-metreleptin neutralizing antibodies and lymphoma; REMS requires prescriber and pharmacy certification

advisory_committee.vote: EMDAC met 11 December 2013: for generalized lipodystrophy the majority agreed benefits outweighed risks (Vote: Yes=11, No=1); for partial lipodystrophy the committee did not find adequate benefit-risk (Vote: Yes=2, No=10)

summary.text: Metreleptin for lipodystrophy was granted orphan drug status and fast track designation in 2001, and the BLA received a priority review (PDUFA goal date later extended three months after a major amendment). It was approved on the basis of open-label, single-arm NIH trials and was approved only for generalized lipodystrophy, with a REMS; the advisory committee supported benefit-risk for generalized but not partial lipodystrophy.

requirement.text: A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) of patients treated with Myalept, regardless of indication, to evaluate serious risks including pancreatitis, hepatic events, severe hypoglycemia, hypersensitivity, serious infections, autoimmune disorders, lymphoma, all cancers, exposed pregnancies, and deaths; continuing 10 years from last patient enrollment or September 2029

citations.quote: - A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) of patients treated with Myalept (metreleptin), regardless of indication, to evaluate serious risks related to the use of Myalept (metreleptin), by indication, including: fatal or necrotizing pancreatitis, hepatic adverse events, severe hypoglycemia, serious hypersensitivity reactions, serious infections resulting in hospitalization or death, new diagnoses of autoimmune disorders (for instance, autoimmune hepatitis, glomerulonephritis, lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis), autoimmune disease exacerbation, lymphoma, all cancers (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) by cancer type, exposed pregnancies and pregnancy outcomes, and all deaths (including causes of death). After agreement with FDA on a targeted sample size, the registry will include patients prescribed Myalept (metreleptin) and will continue for 10 years from the date of last patient's enrollment, or September 2029, whichever is later.

requirement.text: Develop, validate, and implement a ligand binding assay to supplement the neutralizing bioassay for presence of neutralizing antibodies in serum of generalized lipodystrophy patients

citations.quote: 2. To develop, validate, and implement a ligand binding assay to supplement the neutralizing bioassay that tests for the presence of neutralizing antibodies in serum samples from patients with generalized lipodystrophy.

requirement.text: Test all banked clinical samples from pivotal trials NIH 991265/20010769 and trial FHA101 for neutralizing antibodies against leptin using the newly developed ligand binding assay and correlate with clinical events

citations.quote: 3. To test all banked clinical samples from pivotal clinical trials NIH 991265/20010769 and trial FHA101 for the presence of neutralizing antibodies against leptin using the ligand binding assay developed and validated under PMR#2, and to correlate neutralizing antibodies with clinical events.

requirement.text: Conduct a study to assess the immunogenicity of Myalept in a relevant number of patients, testing anti-metreleptin and anti-native-leptin binding antibodies and neutralizing activity, following patients with suspected loss of efficacy or leptin activity

citations.quote: 4. To conduct a study to assess for the immunogenicity of Myalept (metreleptin) in a relevant number of patients receiving metreleptin. The study should include testing for anti-metreleptin and anti-native human leptin binding antibodies at times when antibody responses peak, using a validated assay. The presence of neutralizing antibodies should be assessed using a validated cell-based assay and a validated ligand-binding assay in samples that are confirmed positive for binding antibodies to leptin. All patients with suspected loss of metreleptin efficacy (e.g., worsening glycemic control, increases in triglycerides) or loss of endogenous leptin activity (e.g., severe infections) should be tested for neutralizing activity and followed at least until antibody levels revert to baseline. Antibody titers, neutralizing activity, and associated clinical events should be characterized over time.

requirement.text: An assessment and analysis of spontaneous reports of serious risks (pancreatitis, hepatic events, severe hypoglycemia, hypersensitivity, serious infections, autoimmune disorders, all cancers, exposed pregnancies, deaths) regardless of indication for 10 years from approval

citations.quote: 5. An assessment and analysis of spontaneous reports of serious risks related to the use of Myalept (metreleptin) including: fatal or necrotizing pancreatitis, hepatic adverse events, severe hypoglycemia, serious hypersensitivity reactions, serious infections resulting in hospitalization or death, new diagnoses of autoimmune disorders (for instance, autoimmune hepatitis, glomerulonephritis, lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis), autoimmune disease exacerbation, all cancers (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) by cancer type, exposed pregnancies and pregnancy outcomes, and all deaths (including causes of death) in patients treated with Myalept (metreleptin) regardless of indication for 10 years from the date of approval.

requirement.text: Confirm the in-use stability of metreleptin drug product reconstituted in bacteriostatic water for injection with 0.9% benzyl alcohol using three additional drug product lots, to assess aggregate formation

citations.quote: 7. To confirm the in-use stability of metreleptin drug product (DP) reconstituted in bacteriostatic water for injection containing 0.9% benzyl alcohol (BFWI) with data derived from three additional DP lots, to assess aggregate formation which can impact immunogenicity.

requirement.text: Develop, validate, and implement a suitable assay for assessment of the genetic stability of the metreleptin Working Cell Bank (WCB)

citations.quote: 8. To develop, validate, and implement a suitable assay for the assessment of the genetic stability of metreleptin Working Cell Bank (WCB).

requirement.text: Develop, validate, and implement a qPCR method to detect E. coli DNA impurities in drug substance lots

citations.quote: 9. To develop, validate, and implement the quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) method to detect *E.coli* DNA impurities in drug substance lots. Information demonstrating successful additional validation of the current method may be provided in lieu of developing, validating, and implementing a new method. The revised specification together with the validation information will be submitted to your BLA in accordance with 21 CFR 601.12.

requirement.text: Revise drug product release and stability specification acceptance limits for purity/impurities (RP-HPLC), metreleptin content (UV), potency, and total oligomer content using data from 20 production-scale lots

citations.quote: 10. To revise Myalept drug product (DP) release and stability specifications acceptance limits for: purity and impurities by reverse phase-high performance liquid chromatography RP-HPLC, metreleptin content by ultra-violet (UV) Spectrophotometry and potency using water for injection (WFI) as diluent and total oligomer content after reconstitution with bacteriostatic WFI containing 0.9% benzyl alcohol (BWFI). Data collected from 20 production scale Myalept DP lots and knowledge about the clinical importance of product quality attributes will be used to justify the revised acceptance criteria. The revised specifications together with supporting information will be submitted to your BLA in accordance with 21 CFR 601.12.

requirement.text: Characterize subvisible particles in metreleptin drug product for release, stability, and under forced/stressed degradation conditions, to assess risk and propose a control strategy

citations.quote: 11. To characterize subvisible particles (SVPs) in the [REDACTED](b) (4) size range in metreleptin drug product for release, stability, and under forced or stressed degradation conditions. Results of these studies will be used to assess the risk of SVPs to patients and propose an appropriate strategy for controlling SVP.

requirement.text: Develop a two-tiered reference material system (primary and working RMs) representative of clinical trial and production material

citations.quote: 12. To develop a two-tiered reference material (RM) system comprised of a primary and working RMs that are representative of clinical trial and production material. The working RM will be used for testing of production lots and will be calibrated against the primary reference material.

requirement.text: Assess the impact of drug product container closure extractables and leachables on product quality

To assess the impact of drug product container closure extractables and leachables on product quality, by (1) determining the extractable substances of both the stopper and vials containing reconstituted drug product (b) (4) and (2) providing detailed data (number of tested vials, method description) on leachable studies to support the summary results in Table 4a-1, submitted on November 7, 2013, as part of your response to the FDA information requests (IR) sent on October 8, 2013.
